newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open strong on Wall St highs.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open strong on Wall St highs.

text.p: The Australian share market opened higher on Monday, following Wall Street's record high on Friday, and the local market is likely to continue to look for offshore leads this week as the corporate reporting season ends.
The All Ordinaries index was 21.50 points up at 2,273.80. September share price index futures were 22 points higher at 2,273, narrowing the discount to underlying index to less than a point.
"It's just following on from the (Wall) Street," one Sydney-based broker said. The local market was also continuing the uptrend started Friday after falls earlier last week.

"Apart from that (Wall St's rise) it looks like it could be a quiet week, as the reporting season is out of the way...and there was not much economic data around, either here or offshore," the broker said.
He said BHP's first quarter results, due on Friday, would be the highlight of the corporate week, while local merchandise import data on Wednesday is seen as the main economic figure.

The market lift was underpinned by market heavyweights BHP and CRA Ltd, while the banking sector was the strongest sector. The only stocks to go against the uptrend were engineering stocks and the solid fuels index.
